The most foundational argument against the 22nd Amendment is deceptively simple: in a democracy, the people should decide who leads them. The amendment effectively tells the American electorate, "We don't trust your judgment after two terms." This is paternalism codified into constitutional law.

The modern presidency is arguably the most complex executive position in human history. The learning curve is immense.
